source: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e, Chapter 8: Confidence Intervals (Review Questions & Traps)

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: A point estimate is best defined as ________.
choices: a single number calculated from a sample used to estimate a population parameter
a range of values within which a population parameter is believed to fall
the probability that a sample statistic equals the population mean
the standard deviation of the sampling distribution
questions.correct_answer: a single number calculated from a sample used to estimate a population parameter

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: The confidence level represents ________.
choices: the probability that a specific calculated interval contains the population parameter
the proportion of repeated samples whose confidence intervals will contain the true population parameter
the percentage error tolerated in the point estimate
the degree of freedom associated with the normal distribution
questions.correct_answer: the proportion of repeated samples whose confidence intervals will contain the true population parameter

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: When the sample size n increases while keeping the confidence level constant, what happens to the confidence interval?
choices: The error bound increases, making the confidence interval wider
The error bound decreases, making the confidence interval narrower
The error bound remains identical but shifts toward zero
questions.correct_answer: The error bound decreases, making the confidence interval narrower

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: When constructing a confidence interval for the mean mu of a population and the population standard deviation sigma is known, which distribution must be used?
choices: Student's t-distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: When using the sample size formula n = (z^2 * sigma^2) / EBM^2, how should a fractional result for n always be rounded?
choices: Round to the nearest integer using standard mathematical rounding
Always round UP to the next higher integer to ensure the sample size is large enough
Round DOWN to the lower integer to conserve sample resources
Keep the fractional value for sample weighting
questions.correct_answer: Always round UP to the next higher integer to ensure the sample size is large enough

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: When constructing a confidence interval for the mean mu of a population where the population standard deviation sigma is unknown, which distribution should be used?
choices: Student's t-distribution using sample standard deviation s
standard normal distribution using s directly as sigma
questions.correct_answer: Student's t-distribution using sample standard deviation s

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: For a confidence interval for the mean mu of a population based on a sample of size n where sigma is unknown, the degrees of freedom for the Student's t-distribution are ________.

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: Compared to the standard normal distribution, the Student's t-distribution has ________.
choices: more probability in its tails and thicker tails, reflecting greater variability
a higher peak at the center with zero tail variance
questions.correct_answer: more probability in its tails and thicker tails, reflecting greater variability

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: In a survey estimating a population proportion, if x represents the number of successes in a sample of size n, the point estimate p' is given by ________.

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: The 'plus four' method for calculating confidence intervals for a population proportion should be used when ________.
choices: the population standard deviation is strictly known
the confidence level is at least 90% and the sample size is at least ten
the number of successes equals zero
questions.correct_answer: the confidence level is at least 90% and the sample size is at least ten

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: In the 'plus four' method, what hypothetical adjustment is made to the study trials?
choices: Add four successes to x and four to n
Add four failures to the sample without changing x
Imagine four additional trials: two successes and two failures (add 2 to x and 4 to n)
Multiply both x and n by a factor of 1.04
questions.correct_answer: Imagine four additional trials: two successes and two failures (add 2 to x and 4 to n)

questions.section: 8.4 Confidence Intervals & Calculating Sample Size
questions.question: When calculating the required sample size n to estimate a population proportion without a preliminary estimate of p', what values should be used for p' and q' to ensure a conservative, sufficiently large sample?

questions.section: 8.0 Introduction
questions.question: According to Chapter 8, which exact year did Jerzy Neyman first publish his foundational paper introducing confidence intervals in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 teaches confidence interval procedures without historical citation or publication years of Jerzy Neyman's 1937 paper.

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: In Section 8.2, what specific critical threshold for the Anderson-Darling normality test statistic must the sample data satisfy before applying the Student's t-distribution?
questions.trap_rationale: Section 8.2 assumes underlying normality or large n, but never mentions the Anderson-Darling goodness-of-fit test.

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: According to Chapter 8, what is the maximum recommended BCa (bias-corrected and accelerated) bootstrap iteration count when sample skewness exceeds 0.8?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 covers parametric intervals (z and t) and never mentions bootstrap resampling or BCa intervals.

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: In Section 8.3, what exact non-coverage probability adjustment is prescribed by the Clopper-Pearson exact binomial confidence interval formula?
choices: Poisson tail approximation with continuity correction
questions.trap_rationale: Section 8.3 teaches standard normal approximation and plus-four, but never mentions the Clopper-Pearson exact interval.

questions.section: 8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
questions.question: According to Section 8.1, what specific penalty factor must be multiplied into the margin of error when time-series observations exhibit an autoregressive lag-1 coefficient phi of 0.4?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 strictly assumes independent random samples and never discusses autoregressive time-series autocorrelation adjustments.

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: What is the recommended prior hyperparameter beta(alpha=1, beta=1) credible interval quantile prescribed in Chapter 8 for estimating posterior binomial parameters?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 is purely frequentist and contains zero discussion of Bayesian priors, credible intervals, or posterior distributions.

questions.section: 8.4 Confidence Intervals & Calculating Sample Size
questions.question: According to Section 8.4, what minimum sample size n is required under the Bonferroni inequality correction when constructing simultaneous 95% confidence intervals across 5 independent population means?
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 covers single population mean and proportion sample sizes, without family-wise error rate or Bonferroni adjustments.

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: In Section 8.2, what degrees-of-freedom formula does Chapter 8 specify when using Welch's t-interval for two unequal population variances?
choices: Harmonic mean of degrees of freedom
Pooled variance degrees of freedom n1 + n2 - 2
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 is titled 'Confidence Intervals' for a single population mean/proportion. Two-sample Welch intervals are not in Chapter 8.

questions.section: 8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student's t Distribution
questions.question: What specific bandwidth adjustment does Chapter 8 recommend when using kernel density estimation to verify sample symmetry prior to Student's t calculation?
choices: Silverman's rule of thumb h = 0.9 * A * n^(-1/5)
questions.trap_rationale: Chapter 8 does not mention kernel density estimation, bandwidth selection, or non-parametric density smoothing.

questions.section: 8.3 A Population Proportion
questions.question: According to Chapter 8, which 2023 study by Henderson & Morales demonstrated that plus-four intervals have empirical coverage of 94.8% on micro-survey samples of size n=8?
questions.trap_rationale: OpenStax does not cite a 2023 Henderson & Morales paper; it notes computer studies demonstrated effectiveness without citing specific 2023 papers.
